title: Stated preference methods

definition.text: Valuation methods that measure what people value by asking them directly in surveys, rather than watching what they buy.

facts.text: Contingent valuation, which asks people their willingness to pay for an ecosystem or one of its services, is the best-known stated preference method.
Non-use values are usually estimated with stated preference methods such as contingent valuation or choice modelling, because people's market behaviour reveals nothing about them.
Ecosystem valuation divides its methods into stated preference and revealed preference families.
Conjoint analysis and choice modelling are also used for stated preference research, and David Hensher and Jordan Louviere are credited with the first stated preference choice models.
Many economists distrust stated preferences and prefer people's revealed preferences in binding market transactions when judging willingness to pay.
Revealed and stated preference data can be combined to get the advantages of both.

contested_note: Many economists question whether survey answers can be trusted to measure willingness to pay.
notes: Phrase concept with no page of its own.

title: Benefit transfer

definition.text: A valuation method that estimates a project's benefits by borrowing the data, models and results of earlier studies of similar projects or sites.

facts.text: It comes in two forms: value transfer moves a single unit value from an earlier site, while function transfer uses valuation functions drawn from many studies and can be more accurate.
Meta-analysis can be used to build a valuation transfer.
Its common errors are measurement error, from biased study selection and assumptions, and transfer error, when the original and new sites do not correspond.
It is a cheap way to value a project when time and money rule out original research.

notes: Phrase concept; drafted on the Shadow price section that covers it.

title: Defensive expenditures

definition.text: Money people spend to protect themselves from possible harm, as counted in environmental accounting.

facts.text: Standard accounts do not subtract spending to fight 'bads'; the Index of Sustainable Economic Welfare does subtract private defensive expenditures.
In one study of environmental valuation in project appraisal, defensive expenditures were often usable evidence, though market and proxy prices supplied most of it.

notes: Drafted for the phrase concept 'Averting behavior method'; no sentence describes the averting-behaviour valuation method itself, so it is listed as a gap.
